sections.kicker: Prepared for Austin Motherhood Photographer by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: You told us you are not for everyone. Your homepage is written for everyone.
sections.keep: Your service list includes "loss & grief." Very few photographers say that out loud.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things
people meet

pins.quote: Your family fairytale is getting a whole new chapter.
pins.why: You said you are not for everyone; a fairytale is the most for everyone idea in family photography.
pins.how: Say your actual view of motherhood in the first line, even if it puts some people off.
pins.label: Your site
pins.cost: You attract clients who want the same photos as everyone, and lose the ones who want yours.

pins.what: The name is a search phrase.
pins.why: It tells Google what you are, but not who you are or why you.
pins.how: Keep the phrase for search and give the brand a name and voice of its own.
pins.label: Your name
pins.cost: You compete with every photographer typing the same words.

pins.what: Loss and grief sit quietly at the end of the list.
pins.why: It is where your unique perspective shows: you photograph the hard parts too.
pins.how: Let that honesty shape the headline and the whole voice.
pins.label: Your services
pins.cost: The proof that you are different reads like one more service.

sections.intro: You wrote that you want to stand out for a unique perspective on motherhood and that you are not for everyone. Here is where the site says the opposite.
